newsitem.title: USA: White House says Mubarak will not attend summit.
newsitem.headline: White House says Mubarak will not attend summit.

text.p: Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak will not attend the Middle East crisis summit in Washington being organized by U.S. President Bill Clinton, the White House said on Monday.

"It is not possible for President Mubarak to be here for these discussions. They (the Egyptians) will be following the deliberations very closely," said White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry in announcing expectations for the arrivals of the Middle Eastern leaders invited by Clinton.

Clearly trying to head off speculation Mubarak's absence might indicate a rift between Washington and Cairo, McCurry said the Egyptian leader had "a scheduling conflict" and stressed that Clinton valued his views on Middle East peace.

"The president had a very good (telephone) conversation a short while ago with President Mubarak," McCurry said. "The president is a very valued partner in the peace process as you know and President Clinton often discusses with him matters related to the peace process." He added: "We will be closely engaged with the Egyptians."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein were en route to Washington to discuss ways to halt violence that has killed 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis since last week. The summit was scheduled to take place on Tuesday and Wednesday.
